newsitem.title: INDIA: Merger with India ICICI a bail out for SCICI - Prime.
newsitem.headline: Merger with India ICICI a bail out for SCICI - Prime.

text.p: The proposed merger of Indian term lending bank SCICI Ltd with the Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India (ICICI) is a "premature bail out for SCICI," securities firm Prime Broking said on Friday.
"SCICI was the smallest financial institution and did not have the necessary critical mass to raise wholesale funds at the finest rates," Prime analyst Amit Rajpal said in a study.
"In fact the merger is a premature bail out for SCICI."
The report said SCICI consistently borrowed at rates which were 50 basis points higher than its competitors.

"In a business of thin spreads this differential was critical to the long-term viability of the corporation. In addition, SCICI did not enjoy significant brand equity amongst retail investors," Prime said.
SCICI therefore found it difficult to raise substantial amounts from the retail market, it said.
On the face of it, the merger seems to benefit ICICI on two broad counts -- one being the merger ratio and second, the extinguishing of ICICI's equity holding in SCICI.

"The 1996/97 (April-March) expected EPS for the corporation has increased from 12.06 rupees to 13.04 rupees purely on account of the merger, similarly, the book value has increased from 82 rupees to 88 rupees per share," Prime said.
It cited the following benefits of merger for ICICI:

+ Reduced cost of intermediation: The merger will result in a 25 percent increase in asset base, but only a 10 percent increase in the employees of ICICI. This would result in increased operational efficiency for ICICI.
"However, the flip side is that payscales in SCICI are lower than ICICI on an average and a rationalisation of pay scales would result in higher overall costs to the organisation."

+ Diversification of income stream: Fee income accounted for a higher proportion of SCICI's operating income. Hence the merger would result in ICICI's income stream having a higher proportion of fee income, thereby further diversifying the income stream.

+ Higher capital adequacy: SCICI had a higher capital adequacy, leading to a higher capital adequacy for the merged entity. "However, the disadvantage is that an excessively high capital adequacy would result in lower returns to shareholders."
Prime said a cleaner loan book, mentioned as one of the beneficial effects of the merger, would be temporary.
It said SCICI's non-performing assets (NPA) are understated on account of a relatively new loan book and its asset quality is not significantly different from that of ICICI.
"When NPAs start catching up with SCICI, there could be a pressure on the earnings of the merged entity on account of higher provisioning requirements," it said.
Prime said the merger would not lead to higher spreads, increased volume growth, sustained reduction in NPA levels, better earning quality or improved return on investment.
SCICI and ICICI decided to merge earlier this week. The shareholders of ICICI will get two shares of ICICI in exchange for five shares of SCICI, the two firms said.
"The biggest play of the merger was the increase in EPS of ICICI on account of the merger arithmetic working out in its facour," the Prime study said.
"The long eduring benefits of the merger are overstated. We continue to rate the stock an underperformer..."
